paragraphs.text: Groenewegen et al. (2003) studied a large family with atrial standstill. Candidate gene screening identified a novel mutation in the SCN5A gene, D1275N. The mutation was present in all 3 affected living relatives and in 5 unaffected relatives, and the deceased affected relative was an obligate carrier. SCN5A-D1275N channels showed a small depolarizing shift in activation compared with wildtype channels. In the same family, the authors detected 2 closely linked polymorphisms in regulatory regions of the atrial-specific gap junction gene connexin-40 (Cx40; GJA5), at nucleotides -44 (G-A) and +71 (A-G). Eight relatives were homozygous for both polymorphisms, 3 of whom were affected. This genotype was found in only about 7% of controls. In reporter gene analysis, the rare Cx40 genotype gave reduced expression compared with the more common genotype. The 3 living affected relatives were the only family members who carried both the SCN5A mutation and the rare homozygous Cx40 genotype.

paragraphs.text: In a boy with congenital atrial standstill, Makita et al. (2005) identified a novel SCN5A mutation, L212P, inherited from his father, who was in normal sinus rhythm. The L212P sodium channel was expressed in a heterologous system and studied by whole-cell patch clamp. It showed large hyperpolarizing shifts in the voltage dependence of activation (-63.5 vs -48.1 mV) and of inactivation (-95.6 vs -86.6 mV), as well as delayed recovery from inactivation. The proband, but not his father, also carried Cx40 polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother.
